title: Extrinsic nonlinear spin currents in spin-orbit coupled systems: A Boltzmann transport study
abstract: We develop a semiclassical Boltzmann framework for second-order extrinsic spin transport in the presence of skew scattering. The conventional relaxation-time approximation reduces the full collision integral to a single phenomenological timescale and thereby neglects the angular structure of impurity scattering. While the transport relaxation time primarily characterizes the leading angular harmonic of the nonequilibrium distribution, nonlinear response is sensitive to its higher angular harmonics, which are governed by distinct components of the collision operator. We therefore retain the angular and band dependence of the scattering kernel and decompose both the collision integral and the distribution function into Fourier harmonics. The resulting coupled algebraic equations allow the symmetric and skew-scattering corrections to the distribution function to be obtained recursively order by order in the electric field. We apply this formalism to the gapped surface states of a topological insulator with spin-dependent impurity scattering and evaluate the corresponding second-order extrinsic spin-current response. Our results show that higher angular harmonics of the nonequilibrium distribution and scattering between distinct constant-energy contours play an essential role in extrinsic nonlinear spin transport beyond the single-relaxation-time approximation.
summary: This work develops a sophisticated Boltzmann transport theory to calculate nonlinear spin currents in topological insulators, moving beyond simple relaxation-time approximations. By expanding the distribution function in angular Fourier harmonics, the authors show that higher-order harmonics are crucial for capturing the full physics of spin transport. The methodology provides a systematic way to analyze complex, non-equilibrium transport phenomena in SOC materials.
main_problem: The study addresses the limitations of the single-relaxation-time approximation when calculating extrinsic nonlinear spin currents in spin-orbit coupled systems.
main_result: Higher angular harmonics of the non-equilibrium distribution and scattering between distinct constant-energy contours are shown to be essential for accurately describing extrinsic nonlinear spin transport.
method: The authors employ a semiclassical Boltzmann transport framework, decomposing the collision integral and the distribution function into Fourier harmonics to solve coupled algebraic equations recursively.
model_or_system: The analysis is applied to the gapped surface states of a topological insulator, modeled by a specific Hamiltonian involving spin-orbit coupling and a gap term.
key_observables: Second-order extrinsic spin-current response coefficient ($\Gamma_{\ell, 	ext{ext}}^{ijl}$), and the angular harmonics ($\ell=1, 2$) of the distribution function.
important_parameters: The ratio $mv^2/\Delta$ dictates the scattering regime (monotonic vs. nonmonotonic band structure).
main_assumptions: The analysis neglects the contribution of the skew-scattering part to the second-order distribution function and assumes elastic impurity scattering, which limits the relaxation of the $l=0$ harmonic.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the recursive solution procedure, the band structures for different parameter regimes, and the calculated second-order extrinsic spin-current coefficients in the nonmonotonic regime.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the Boltzmann equation solution by expanding the distribution function in Fourier harmonics, solving coupled equations for different harmonics, and finally calculating the second-order spin current coefficients.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter transport, the rigorous, non-equilibrium, harmonic expansion technique for solving the Boltzmann equation is a powerful theoretical tool applicable to open quantum systems dynamics.
